answer: Continuous proof-of-work per epoch resists sybils: standing is not granted once at a summit and kept, it must be re-mined every cycle by solving a fresh unpredictable task. Each vertex in a fake farm must independently forge new compute each epoch; there is no shared shortcut because the challenge is seeded per identity. Ten thousand clones therefore owe ten thousand ongoing computations forever, so a one-time setup never converts into lasting free influence.
